newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark not ready to join Nordic power bourse - report.
newsitem.headline: Denmark not ready to join Nordic power bourse - report.

text.p: Legal and infrastructure problems mean that it could be a long time before Denmark can join a proposed Nordic electricity exchange, a Danish electricity industry newspaper wrote on Thursday.

"In Denmark there will have to be a series of organisational changes to establish compatible supply systems, moves to open networks to potential outside suppliers and the abolition of ties between producers and distribution," Elsam Posten said.
A Norwegian-Swedish electricity exchange was set up in January 1996 and there are plans to expand it to a Nordic bourse.
The paper, published by Elsam, Denmark's largest electricity producer, said that Denmark must make major organisational and regulatory changes to qualify for participation.

"Unlike Denmark, Finland is now almost ready to participate in the proposed joint Nordic electricity exchange. The necessary legislation is in place and it fits in well with the Norwegian and Swedish electricity markets," Elsam Posten said.

"If Danish electricity companies fail to take the necessary initiatives, Denmark will not be able to join the Nordic electricity bourse along with Finland," Elsam's Uffe Steiner Jensen told the newspaper.
Jensen recommended that Denmark join the Nordic exchange rather than wait for the establishment of an European electricity bourse.
Elsam has been a member of the Norwegian-Swedish exchange for the past year.
